w10_T4_002290: Nadia records her golf practice in minutes rather than in hours, because her coach prefers it that way. On Monday morning her logbook showed 171 minutes for the week. During the afternoon she added 29 minutes on the driving range, and in the evening she added another 40 minutes of putting practice. Her coach then found that 174 of the logged minutes belonged to an earlier week and struck them off. The minutes that were left were divided equally between 2 report cards, one for the club and one for her school. How many minutes were written on one report card?
w10_T4_002293: Marcus assembles 75 badges every hour at the workshop, and last Friday he worked for 9 hours straight. He packed the whole day's output into 3 identical crates, with the same number of badges in each crate. Dana, who runs the sister workshop, ordered 6 crates of exactly that size for a conference. The two of them joked that Dana's single order was larger than anything Marcus had ever built in a day. Sadly, 254 badges in Dana's order came out with the wrong logo and were thrown away. The workshop has been open for 12 years. How many usable badges were in Dana's order?
w10_T4_002295: Aisha's nursery started the season with 138 seedling trays, but a late frost ruined 36 of them. Every remaining tray was planted with 6 tomato seedlings. A neighbouring farm donated 74 extra seedlings, and later that month 302 seedlings were sold at the market. The greenhouse is 45 metres long, and the staff always record their watering times in minutes rather than in hours. Each seedling Aisha still has is expected to produce 9 tomatoes. How many tomatoes should the nursery expect from its seedlings?
w10_T4_002301: Ravi writes his trip savings down in dollars rather than in cents. On Monday morning his tin held 86 dollars. In the afternoon he spent 10 dollars on a bus pass, and then he split everything that was left into 4 equal shares, one for himself and one for each of his cousins, keeping only his own share. That evening he earned 24 dollars washing cars, and on Tuesday he paid 34 dollars for a museum ticket. At the fair, every dollar he still had could be exchanged for 2 ride tokens, and he exchanged the whole lot. How many ride tokens did Ravi receive?
w10_T4_002308: Each morning the Larkspur Cafe bakes 120 muffins for the counter, and the head baker sets aside 5 more for the staff room. The cafe repeated exactly that routine on each of the 9 days of the town festival. Over the festival 348 of those muffins went stale and were thrown out. A neighbouring bakery then sent over 49 muffins to help with the final rush. The cafe prints its prices in dollars rather than in cents. Before opening on the first day it had handed out a dozen free samples that were never counted in the baking records. How many muffins did the cafe have at the end of the festival?
w10_T4_002317: Nora seals 141 pencils into every box at the depot. Each carton holds 3 of those boxes, every pallet holds 4 cartons, and each truck is loaded with 4 pallets. Before a truck leaves, Felix always tosses in 52 loose pencils as spares, so his trucks carry more than Nora's boxes alone account for. On Friday 8 identical trucks left the depot, each one loaded and topped up in exactly that way. The depot's roof was repaired 6 years ago. How many pencils left the depot on Friday?
w10_T4_002322: On Saturday morning the corner shop had 60 jars of marbles on its shelf. A delivery van dropped off 45 more jars before lunch, and during the lunch rush 102 jars were sold. In the afternoon a second delivery added 72 jars to the shelf. Every jar still on the shelf that evening contained exactly 8 marbles. Each of those marbles was worth 6 points in the shop's Saturday game. How many points were sitting on the shelf that evening?
w10_T4_002334: Elena's tile workshop had 166 boxes of tiles in the yard, and Marcus delivered 20 more boxes, though he arrived half an hour late. The boxes were then shared equally among 3 building sites, and Elena's site took one share. At Elena's site 59 boxes turned out to be water damaged and were sent back to the supplier. Every box still at her site holds 6 trays. Each of those trays holds 8 tiles. How many tiles does Elena's site have?
w10_T4_002337: At the Riverside charity walk, each of the 117 walkers raised 9 dollars from sponsors. A bake stall at the finish line brought in another 47 dollars. The route passed a dozen village halls along the river. All of the money raised was then divided equally among 5 local charities. The animal shelter, one of those charities, immediately spent 175 dollars on winter feed. How many dollars did the animal shelter have left?
w10_T4_002339: Owen's recycling depot started the week with 198 crates of bottles, and his colleague Priya brought in 43 more, which was far fewer than Owen had collected on his own. Each of the depot's 4 lorries was then loaded with exactly that many crates. On the motorway 107 crates were damaged beyond use. A supermarket took 462 crates from the lorries, and a bottling plant collected another 154. How many crates were still on the lorries?
w10_T4_002343: Early on Saturday morning Leo found 12 cookies left over in the tin. By late morning he and Mia had baked 75 more. During the afternoon 55 cookies were sold at their stall. In the evening the cookies that remained were split into 2 equal shares, one for Leo and one for Mia, and Leo carried his share home. Overnight his family ate 15 of Leo's cookies. At breakfast he cut each cookie he had left into 4 equal pieces. How many pieces did Leo have?
w10_T4_002346: A print shop received 3 crates of blank notebooks, with 52 notebooks in each crate. It sold 147 of the notebooks that week, and then 67 unsold notebooks came back from a nearby school. Every notebook in the shop has 8 sheets of paper, and every sheet has 2 sides that can be printed on. The old press has been running for 14 years, and its speed is logged in minutes rather than in hours. So far 919 of those printable sides have been used. How many printable sides are still blank?
w10_T4_002347: At dawn a farmer divided 144 apples equally among his 6 market stalls. At the stall by the fountain, the morning delivery van added 51 more apples. Just after noon a neighbour dropped off another 11 apples at that same stall. By evening the fountain stall had sold every one of its apples at 4 rupees each. How many rupees did the fountain stall take that day?
w10_T4_002356: Mara planted 13 rows of carrots with 9 plants in every row. She later added 20 more seedlings to the same plot. She harvested 94 of the plants in August, rabbits destroyed 18 more, and she gave 4 plants to a neighbour. Her shed sits half a mile down the lane, and she has been gardening this plot for 15 years. Every plant still growing will produce 6 carrots. How many carrots can Mara still expect?
w10_T4_002358: A restorer received 166 crates of mosaic tiles, with 8 tiles in each crate. She found that 821 of the tiles were cracked and set them aside. Each tile she can still use is decorated with 5 small glass stones. During the move 2096 of those stones fell out and were lost. The mosaic wall is 12 metres wide, and the workshop always records weights in grams rather than in kilograms. Each stone that remains weighs 9 grams. What is the total weight, in grams, of the stones that remain?
w10_T4_002360: The radio station writes its schedule in minutes rather than in hours. For each of the 7 days of festival week, 230 minutes of music were planned. A special interview added another 71 minutes to the week's plan. By Friday night 1464 of the planned minutes had already been broadcast. The producer then cut 31 minutes from what was still to come. How many minutes of the plan were left?
w10_T4_002361: Nina started the term with 95 stickers, and she traded 93 of them away to Owen, who ended up with far more stickers than she had. Owen felt guilty and gave her enough new ones to triple what she was still holding. Nina then split her stickers into 3 equal piles and kept only one pile, giving the others to her sisters. She lost 1 sticker on the walk home. At the weekend she bought 36 more. How many stickers does Nina have now?
w10_T4_002373: Jonah rode 46 kilometres on each of the 5 days of his training camp. On the Saturday afterwards he rode another 44 kilometres. On Sunday morning he added 8 kilometres of warm-up laps, and on Sunday afternoon he rode a further 58 kilometres. His club records ride times in minutes rather than in hours, which fills his logbook with large numbers. How many kilometres did Jonah ride in total?
w10_T4_002377: A church hall received 154 boxes of candles, and each box held 5 candles. A second delivery arrived that afternoon and doubled the number of candles in the store. A volunteer then donated 73 more candles. The hall counts its stock in single candles rather than in boxes, which the warden finds tedious. Over Christmas 540 candles were burned, and afterwards 33 unused candles were returned from the chapel. The hall itself was built 92 years ago. How many candles are in the store now?
w10_T4_002382: Early in the morning a baker divided 30 kilograms of flour equally among his 3 ovens. Working with the flour set aside for one oven, he baked 4 loaves from every kilogram. In the afternoon each of those loaves was cut into 6 slices. He then packed all of that oven's slices equally into 5 paper bags. In the evening a school party ate 43 slices from one of those bags. The bakery weighs its flour in kilograms rather than in grams. How many slices were left in that bag?
w10_T4_002383: Dev had gathered 78 signatures for the park petition by Friday. His friend Rosa added 35 more at the school gate, and a market stall brought in another 65, so Rosa's own contribution was smaller than Dev's. The campaign ran in 7 towns altogether, and every town collected exactly the same number of signatures as Dev's town did. The organisers count the deadline in days rather than in weeks, which makes it feel closer. A final check found that 380 of all the signatures collected were invalid. How many valid signatures did the campaign have?
w10_T4_002388: A builder ordered 186 pallets of bricks, and every pallet carried 4 bundles. A neighbouring site sent over 50 spare bundles, and the supplier later added 75 more. Each bundle on the site contains 8 bricks. Half of the site is still fenced off for the diggers. The crew used 2794 bricks on the garden wall. How many bricks are left on the site?
w10_T4_002392: Hannah had 148 photographs in her album, and her brother Sam gave her 57 more from his own smaller collection. She then removed 72 blurred photographs and threw them away. At the print shop she made copies until she held triple the number of photographs she had after that clear-out. Her aunt later sent 64 more prints in the post. How many photographs does Hannah have now?
w10_T4_002396: A drinks depot began the month with 230 crates and took in 52 more from the bottling plant. Every crate in the depot holds 7 packs. Each pack contains 6 cans, and the depot always counts its stock in single cans rather than in crates. During the summer sale exactly half of all those cans were sold. How many cans were still in the depot?
w10_T4_002398: A small museum's store held 229 old display cases, and 221 of them were sent away to another museum. Each case that stayed behind holds 5 fossils. A collector then donated 11 more fossils to the museum. The curator photographs every fossil in the collection from 6 different angles. A dozen visitors waited outside while she worked. How many photographs does the curator take?
